purpose: This is the SECOND, independent cost measurement (decisions.md's Epic 5 pricing input). Core Rulebook (Epic 3, artifacts/epic-3-core-rulebook/step-cost-ledger.json) is deep and many-bucketed -- 970 starting bucket-B units across 29 distinct mechanisms. Ultimate Campaign is shallow and single-bucketed -- exactly one bucket-B mechanism (5 units) closed it. Two books of opposite shape give Epic 5 a range, not one blended number.

measurement_method.wall_time: commit-to-commit timestamp span between the immediately prior commit touching docs/work-inventory.json and this cycle's own commit, via `git log --reverse --format=%H|%ct|%s ea2b3396f2..HEAD -- docs/work-inventory.json` -- same instrument and same UPPER-BOUND caveat as step-cost-ledger.json for core_rulebook (the span also carries queue/dispatch overhead between cycles, including the intervening AT-34-E4-001 proof-only cycle which touched no docs/work-inventory.json commit).
measurement_method.units_cleared: docs/work-inventory.json checked out at the commit before and at the commit itself (`git show <sha>:docs/work-inventory.json`), partitioned both times with the live `completion_atlas.partition(units, book='ultimate_campaign')` function -- the same code the standing gate runs, not a re-implementation.
measurement_method.bucket_attribution: the one Epic-4 commit touching docs/work-inventory.json (4005925ae2) is self-tagged AT-34-E4-002 / bucket B in its own commit message and receipt.
measurement_method.redrive_command: git log --reverse --format='%H|%ct|%s' ea2b3396f2..HEAD -- docs/work-inventory.json (full list in step-cost-ledger-raw-commits.json); python3 scripts/completion_atlas.py --book ultimate_campaign --check at HEAD for the current partition.

dominant_mechanism.name: AT-34-E4-002 PI-coordinate wire-up for Kind::Trait (reused decisions.md §14 mechanism, already built for Kind::Domain/Kind::Deity)

B.meaning: table exists, record not in it (BUCKET_DEFINITIONS['B'])
B.closure_vs_reclassification: of the 5 units that left bucket B, 3 reached DONE (zero-magnitude display-class, real closure) and 2 moved to another unfinished bucket -- 1 to M (real BONUS:SKILL magnitude, a lookup not a compute path) and 1 to D (genuine prose ability-scaling, ambiguous wiring class pending review). Movement recorded per decisions.md §12 L10: a count that drops because measurement changed is not closure -- here 3/5 is real closure, 2/5 is reclassification, both counted honestly rather than the whole 5 claimed as closure.

D.note: no dedicated D-clearing cycle has run; count moved only as a side effect of the bucket-B cycle above (AT-34-E4-002 reclassified 1 unit into it).

M.note: no dedicated M-clearing (compute-and-apply) cycle has run; count grew by 1 as a side effect of the bucket-B cycle above. AT-34-E4-002's own receipt names this bucket's clearing mechanism as real engine work with unmeasured per-unit cost, requiring a sample measurement before any population run.

V.note: no dedicated V-clearing (oracle-harness) cycle has run for ultimate_campaign.

U.note: resolved BY PROOF, not by bucket movement -- AT-34-E4-001 mechanically proved the unmeasurable verdict is correct-and-final for all 21 (decisions.md's own class of legitimate zero-unit-moved deliverable, decisions.md §9). Not a clearing cost in this ledger's units-per-hour sense: 0 units moved, so no rate is defined. Its wall time is real (AT-34-E4-001's own receipt/commits) but produces no bucket-count denominator this ledger can divide by -- reported for completeness, excluded from the rate comparison below rather than forced into a rate of 0.

X.note: resolved BY PROOF as correct-and-final (AT-34-E4-001) -- same non-rate class as U above.

scaffolding_note: AT-34-E4-001's two commits (72c9f6fec6, 68e9b353b9) touch no docs/work-inventory.json commit and so contribute no row to buckets_cleared_so_far -- see step-cost-ledger-raw-commits.json's note_on_AT-34-E4-001. This is not an omission: a cycle that moves zero units in the ledger's own denominator correctly produces no per-unit rate.

epic_3_bucket_B.per_mechanism_minutes_range: 22.2 to 617.4 minutes per cycle (28x spread across 29 distinct mechanisms)

comparison_against_epic_3_rates.where_they_agree: Epic 4's single mechanism (108.0 min, 5 units, 21.6 min/unit-touched) falls squarely inside Epic 3's own per-mechanism range (22.2-617.4 min/cycle) -- it is not an outlier against Epic 3's population of mechanisms, it is a cheap-to-mid mechanism by that same yardstick. The closest size- and shape-matched Epic 3 comparator is 'AT-34-E3-001 domain mechanism' (1 unit, 40.3 min -> 1.49 units/hour DONE) and 'race_trait_race_not_modelled' (9 units, 70.0 min, but 132 net core_rulebook units cleared via a generic table fallback) -- both PI/coordinate-adjacent reattribution mechanisms of the same general kind as Epic 4's fix, and both land in the same 1-2 units/hour-for-DONE-only neighborhood once mixed-bucket destinations (M/D, not all-DONE) are accounted for the same way.
comparison_against_epic_3_rates.where_they_diverge: Epic 4's blended units-per-hour-DONE (1.667) is roughly 3.5x SLOWER than Epic 3's blended bucket-B rate (5.8). Taken at face value this would say Ultimate Campaign is costlier per unit than Core Rulebook, which contradicts the book being 'shallow and single-bucketed.'
comparison_against_epic_3_rates.which_divergence_is_explained_by_book_sh: NOT book shape -- this is a sample-size artifact, stated plainly rather than papered over. Epic 3's 5.8 units/hour is a BLEND across 29 cycles and 503 units, smoothing over its own 28x per-mechanism spread; Epic 4's 1.667 is a single cycle, a single mechanism, 5 units -- exactly the kind of small-n figure decisions.md §12 L11 (measure per-unit cost before a population-scoped run) warns cannot be extrapolated. A single 5-unit sample sitting inside Epic 3's per-mechanism range (as shown above) is fully consistent with Epic 3's own mechanism-level variance; it does not demonstrate Ultimate Campaign's book shape is intrinsically costlier. The one shape-linked (not noise-linked) fact this ledger CAN state: Ultimate Campaign's bucket B needed exactly ONE mechanism to reach zero (closed in a single cycle) where Core Rulebook's bucket B needed 29 -- consistent with the Evidence text's 'shallow and single-bucketed' framing for BUCKET COUNT and MECHANISM COUNT, even though this ledger cannot yet make the same claim for PER-UNIT WALL-TIME COST on a sample of one.
comparison_against_epic_3_rates.headline_finding_for_epic_5: Do not price Ultimate Campaign's remaining buckets (M:89, D:5, V:18) off this single 1.667 units/hour figure -- it is one mechanism's cost, not a book-wide rate, and Epic 3's own ledger shows a single mechanism can be off a book's blended rate by an order of magnitude in either direction. Epic 5 should price Ultimate Campaign's M/D/V buckets from Epic 3's PER-MECHANISM-TYPE rates for the same bucket letter (M, D, V are compute-path / oracle-harness mechanisms, structurally different from bucket B's lookup-wiring mechanisms measured here) once at least one M/D/V-clearing cycle exists for either book, not from this ledger's single bucket-B data point.
